'''Punxsutawney Phil''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|p|ʌ|ŋ|k|s|ə|ˈ|t|ɔː|n|i}}) is a [[groundhog]] residing in [[Young Township, Jefferson County, Pennsylvania|Young Township]] near [[Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania]], United States, who is the central figure in Punxsutawney's annual [[Groundhog Day]] celebration.

== Overview ==
The Punxsutawney Groundhog Day celebration is rooted in [[Germanic mythology|Germanic]] tradition that says that if a hibernating animal casts a shadow on February 2, the Christian celebration of [[Candlemas]], winter and cold weather will last another six weeks. If no shadow is seen, legend says, spring will come early. In Germany, the tradition evolved into a myth that if the sun came out on Candlemas, a [[hedgehog]] would cast its shadow, predicting snow all the way into May.<ref>{{cite web |title=Groundhog Day, Hedgehogs and Candlemas |url=http://www.bellaonline.com/articles/art23627.asp |website=www.bellaonline.com |access-date=February 3, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202235407/http://www.bellaonline.com/articles/art23627.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> When German immigrants settled in Pennsylvania, they transferred the tradition onto local fauna, replacing hedgehogs with groundhogs. Several towns in the region on either side of the US-Canada border hold [[Groundhog Day#Regional celebrations|similar Groundhog Day events]], though Punxsutawney's event is the most famous.

'''Punxsutawney Phil''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|p|ʌ|ŋ|k|s|ə|ˈ|t|ɔː|n|i}}) is a [[groundhog]] residing in [[Young Township, Jefferson County, Pennsylvania|Young Township]] near [[Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania]], United States, who is the central figure in Punxsutawney's annual [[Groundhog Day]] celebration.

== Overview ==
The Punxsutawney Groundhog Day celebration is rooted in [[Germanic mythology|Germanic]] tradition that says that if a hibernating animal casts a shadow on February 2, the Christian celebration of [[Candlemas]], winter and cold weather will last another six weeks. If no shadow is seen, legend says, spring will come early. In Germany, the tradition evolved into a myth that if the sun came out on Candlemas, a [[hedgehog]] would cast its shadow, predicting snow all the way into May.<ref>{{cite web |title=Groundhog Day, Hedgehogs and Candlemas |url=http://www.bellaonline.com/articles/art23627.asp |website=www.bellaonline.com |access-date=February 3, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202235407/http://www.bellaonline.com/articles/art23627.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> When German immigrants settled in Pennsylvania, they transferred the tradition onto local fauna, replacing hedgehogs with groundhogs. Several towns in the region on either side of the US-Canada border hold [[Groundhog Day#Regional celebrations|similar Groundhog Day events]], though Punxsutawney's event is the most famous.

Punxsutawney's annual civic festival is held on February 2 each year.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pennlive.com/life/2020/01/groundhog-day-2020-guide-punxsutawney-phil-facts-tips-for-going-to-gobblers-knob-and-more.html|title=Groundhog Day 2020 Guide: Punxsutawney Phil facts, tips for going to Gobbler's Knob and more|date=January 28, 2020|website=pennlive|language=en|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200212205702/https://www.pennlive.com/life/2020/01/groundhog-day-2020-guide-punxsutawney-phil-facts-tips-for-going-to-gobblers-knob-and-more.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The central event is a ceremony, which begins well before the winter sunrise, where Phil emerges from his temporary home on Gobbler's Knob, located in a rural area about {{convert|2|mi|0}} southeast of the town. According to the tradition, if Phil sees his shadow and returns to his hole, he has predicted six more weeks of [[winter]]-like weather.<ref name="auto" /> If Phil does not see his shadow, he has predicted an "early [[spring (season)|spring]]."<ref name="FAQ">{{cite web |title=Groundhog.org FAQ |work=Groundhog.org |url=http://www.groundhog.org/ |access-date=February 2, 2009 |archive-date=July 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717053947/http://www.groundhog.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The event formally began in 1887, although its roots go back even further.<ref name="Staff">{{Cite web|url=https://www.history.com/news/groundhog-day-history-and-facts|title=Groundhog Day: History and Facts|website=History.com|language=en|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206214521/https://www.history.com/news/groundhog-day-history-and-facts|url-status=live}}</ref> The event, and other groundhog-related events throughout the year,<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Us |url=https://www.groundhog.org/about/ |url-status=live |website=Punxsutawney Groundhog club}}</ref> are organized by the Punxsutawney Groundhog Club's "Inner Circle" – recognizable by their [[top hat]]s and [[tuxedo (clothing)|tuxedos]].

The event is based upon a communal light-hearted [[suspension of disbelief]] which ascribes fantastical abilities to Phil. Ostensibly, Phil communicates his prediction to the president of the Inner Circle, who can magically understand his "Groundhogese" due to possession of an ancient [[acacia]] wood cane.  The president then directs the vice president to read the a corresponding scroll (one is prepared for each potential outcome), announcing Phil's forecast.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lKQhYPcNhx0 |title=Every Day Is Groundhog Day For Punxsutawney Phil’s Caretakers {{!}} TODAY Original |date=February 1, 2020 |last=TODAY |access-date=January 15, 2025 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

The suspension of disbelief extends to the assertion that Phil is infallible, and occasional incorrect predictions are the errors of those in charge of translating the message rather than Phil himself. Empirical estimates place the predictions' accuracy between 35% and 41%.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/news/groundhog-forecasters-versus-us-temperature-record |title=Groundhog Forecaster

== Overview ==
The Punxsutawney Groundhog Day celebration is rooted in [[Germanic mythology|Germanic]] tradition that says that if a hibernating animal casts a shadow on February 2, the Christian celebration of [[Candlemas]], winter and cold weather will last another six weeks. If no shadow is seen, legend says, spring will come early. In Germany, the tradition evolved into a myth that if the sun came out on Candlemas, a [[hedgehog]] would cast its shadow, predicting snow all the way into May.<ref>{{cite web |title=Groundhog Day, Hedgehogs and Candlemas |url=http://www.bellaonline.com/articles/art23627.asp |website=www.bellaonline.com |access-date=February 3, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202235407/http://www.bellaonline.com/articles/art23627.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> When German immigrants settled in Pennsylvania, they transferred the tradition onto local fauna, replacing hedgehogs with groundhogs. Several towns in the region on either side of the US-Canada border hold [[Groundhog Day#Regional celebrations|similar Groundhog Day events]], though Punxsutawney's event is the most famous.

Punxsutawney's annual civic festival is held on February 2 each year.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pennlive.com/life/2020/01/groundhog-day-2020-guide-punxsutawney-phil-facts-tips-for-going-to-gobblers-knob-and-more.html|title=Groundhog Day 2020 Guide: Punxsutawney Phil facts, tips for going to Gobbler's Knob and more|date=January 28, 2020|website=pennlive|language=en|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200212205702/https://www.pennlive.com/life/2020/01/groundhog-day-2020-guide-punxsutawney-phil-facts-tips-for-going-to-gobblers-knob-and-more.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The central event is a ceremony, which begins well before the winter sunrise, where Phil emerges from his temporary home on Gobbler's Knob, located in a rural area about {{convert|2|mi|0}} southeast of the town. According to the tradition, if Phil sees his shadow and returns to his hole, he has predicted six more weeks of [[winter]]-like weather.<ref name="auto" /> If Phil does not see his shadow, he has predicted an "early [[spring (season)|spring]]."<ref name="FAQ">{{cite web |title=Groundhog.org FAQ |work=Groundhog.org |url=http://www.groundhog.org/ |access-date=February 2, 2009 |archive-date=July 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717053947/http://www.groundhog.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The event formally began in 1887, although its roots go back even further.<ref name="Staff">{{Cite web|url=https://www.history.com/news/groundhog-day-history-and-facts|title=Groundhog Day: History and Facts|website=History.com|language=en|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206214521/https://www.history.com/news/groundhog-day-history-and-facts|url-status=live}}</ref> The event, and other groundhog-related events throughout the year,<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Us |url=https://www.groundhog.org/about/ |url-status=live |website=Punxsutawney Groundhog club}}</ref> are organized by the Punxsutawney Groundhog Club's "Inner Circle" – recognizable by their [[top hat]]s and [[tuxedo (clothing)|tuxedos]].

The [[Pennsylvania German language|Pennsylvania German dialect]] is the only language spoken at the event, and those who speak English pay a penalty, usually in the form of a [[nickel (United States coin)|nickel]], [[dime (United States coin)|dime]], or [[quarter (United States coin)|quarter]] per word spoken, with the money put into a bowl in the center of the table.<ref name="rosenberger">{{cite book |last=Rosenberger |first=Homer Tope |title=The Pennsylvania Germans: 1891–1965 |location=Lancaster, PA |publisher=Pennsylvania German Society |year=1966 |pages=194–199 |oclc=1745108}}</ref> In select locations, such as [[Myerstown]] (where Uni is the resident groundhog), if February 2 lands on a Sunday, the ceremonies are moved to February 1.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Toth |first=Matthew |title=Groundhog Day 2025: What did Uni of Lebanon County say? |url=https://www.ldnews.com/story/news/local/2025/02/02/uni-the-groundhog-will-there-be-six-more-weeks-of-winter/78104121007/ |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=Lebanon Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> Most of these celebrations outside of Punxsutawney have switched to taxidermied specimens, stuffed toys or costumed characters instead of a live groundhog as of 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lardani |first=Rachael |date=2026-02-02 |title=ROUNDUP {{!}} Full list of local groundhogs’ hot takes on winter |url=https://www.wgal.com/article/pa-susquehanna-valley-local-groundhog-day-events/70191710 |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=WGAL |language=en}}</ref>

''Chuckles'', a self-proclaimed woodchuck, has been providing the regional weather prognostication in [[Manchester, Connecticut]] since 1968 at the Lutz Children's Museum. According to tradition, Chuckles whispers his prediction into the ear of the town mayor, the only Connecticut public official who speaks "groundhog-ese", who then announces it to a crowd of citizens and state officials including the [[Governor of Connecticut|governor]]. The celebration is traditionally broadcast live by local television station [[WFSB]] and participating radio affiliates. An analysis of historical weather data and Chuckles' previous predictions reveals he offers a 60% accuracy rate, higher than most other weather-predicting animals nationwide. Notably, in 2024, Chuckles predicted an early spring (alongside Punxsutawney Phil and others) but Winter Storm Birch followed soon after, prompting the local police department of [[Guilford, Connecticut]] to issue a warrant and dubbing the rodent "Chuck the Liar". In a show of good will, Chuckles "turned himself in", but his record of previous accuracy and community service allowed him to be released.<ref>{{cite news |title=CT's 'groundhogs' predictions are among the nation's most accurate |url=https://ctmirror.org/2024/02/02/ct-groundhog-day-chuckles-accuracy/ |work=[[The Connecticut Mirror]] |date=2 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=CT's Chuckles, Beardsley Bart, Scramble the Duck make Groundhog Day predictions |url=https://www.wfsb.com/2024/02/02/cts-chuckles-prepares-make-groundhog-day-prediction/ |work=[[WFSB]] |date=2 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Chuckles the Groundhog - A Beloved Tradition |url=https://lutzmuseum.org/chuckles-the-groundhog |publisher=The Lutz Children's Museum}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Groundhog Makes Prediction at the Lutz |url=https://www.manchesterct.gov/Community/Town-Calendar-of-Events/Groundhog-Makes-Prediction-at-the-Lutz |publisher=[[Manchester, Connecticut]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=#FREECHUCKLES: CT's groundhog turns himself into Guilford police |url=https://www.wfsb.com/2024/02/15/guilford-police-say-they-have-warrant-out-arrest-cts-groundhog/ |work=WFSB |date=15 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Conn.'s Chuckles XI prepares to deliver 2025 prognostication after his 'arrest' last year |url=https://theday.com/news/699201/conns-chuckles-xi-prepares-to-deliver-2025-prognostication-after-his-arrest-last-year/# |work=[[The New London Day]] |date=29 January 2025}}</ref>
